page_title: A Simple Web App in Rust, Part 2a

summary.title: A Simple Web App in Rust, Part 2a
summary.one_liner: You learn how to fix common Rust type errors in early code, especially around try! and Result, by reading compiler output and expanding macros with rustc.
takeaways: try! returns early with Err, so it cannot be used in a main that returns unit (()).
rustc --pretty=expanded shows macro-expanded code, which makes errors caused by macros easier to debug.
A function writing to a file can return io::Result<()> and end with Ok(()) to satisfy the type checker.
Using unwrap() is simpler but throws errors away; the author considers the try!/Result approach more idiomatic.
summary.summary: The author, continuing a series on building a simple Rust log app, tries to create and write a file and runs into a string of compiler type errors. They walk through each error, including match arm mismatches, unused-variable warnings, and the problem with try! inside a function returning unit. They use rustc's expanded-macro output to see that try! returns early with Err, then fix the signature to io::Result<()> and end with Ok(()). The post is a candid, beginner-level account of learning Rust's type system through trial and error, and it ends with a working log_something function.
